article_notes: Cross-sectional study at the VTH, Abeokuta, Nigeria: 103 dogs with babesiosis diagnosed by Giemsa thin smear only (Babesia spp., species not identified; B. rossi and B. vogeli occur in Nigeria). 80 were anaemic; 18 died, all anaemic (17.5% of 103; 22.5% of the 80 anaemic dogs). The population is unclear: Methods say exclusions (other infections, bleeding, malnutrition) left 80 dogs, while Results say 80 of 103 were anaemic; outcome comparisons (Table 3) appear to be within the 80 anaemic dogs (18 died vs 62 survived). Follow-up horizon for mortality not stated. Table 3 gives mean ± (SD or SE not stated), independent t-test. Hb unit printed as mg/dl. Table 2 header is garbled by PDF conversion ('T f Anmi', 'ypes o ea'), but the rows can be read; the % in its Dead column are shares of all deaths, not mortality within each group. Table 1 prints '3.2.7' for 32.7. S2 (anaemic vs non-anaemic) is used for the signalment comparisons in Table 1. No healthy control group.

Among the age groups, the percentage of anemia was higher in dogs above 3 years.
